analyst_view.overall: Sunderland (11th, 7 pts) host Jagiellonia (29th, 3 pts) needing a win to stay near the top eight, after a 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb last time in Europe. They drew 0-0 at Aston Villa on Saturday and host Tottenham on Sunday, so changes are likely (Danso, who cannot face his parent club Spurs, is expected to start); Le Bris confirmed that Granit Xhaka (calf) and Brian Brobbey (thigh) miss this game, with Ballard, Mundle and Diarra also out. The numbers count Brobbey (about -23% on Sunderland's goals) and Diarra, but not Xhaka or rotation; Trai Hume is one booking from a ban, not banned, as one page had suggested. Jagiellonia have lost three of four in this phase without scoring in the last two, Ousmane Sow is a doubt with a knock, and their fans are banned by UEFA; Bulgarian referee Georgi Kabakov (about 4.6 cards a game) is already counted. One squad page this evening lists Hume as banned and Jagiellonia captain Taras Romanczuk as suspended, but it mixes in domestic bookings and no second source confirms either, so I do not size them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already take a big slice off Sunderland for Brobbey, with their poor recent scoring (3 in six) also counted. Xhaka's confirmed absence and likely rotation before Spurs are not in the numbers, and Jagiellonia have not scored in their last two European games, so I trim a little, to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 7.2 for Sunderland, already a little lower for their recent corner count. Without Xhaka to set the tempo and with changes likely, Sunderland's pressure should be a bit lighter, so I go only to about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already raised for both sides' recent bookings and for referee Georgi Kabakov's above-average record (4.6 a game). Hume is one yellow from a ban and may be careful, and an empty away end takes some heat out of the game, but neither is strong enough to move, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots, mostly Sunderland (21.3), already up about 8% for their recent shooting. Rotation with Spurs three days later and no Xhaka should trim that a little, so I go to about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, and Sunderland have been wasteful in front of goal lately. A rotated attack, possibly led by Tutierov or Isidor, without Brobbey (counted) or Xhaka's passing (not counted) should be slightly less sharp, so I go to about 9.5.
